  "elsewhere_quote": "Conversely, if $S$ meets every member of $\\mathcal F$, choose an integer $x\\ge a_1$ with support $S$. Every accepted integer smaller than $x$ has support in $\\mathcal F$, and thus is noncoprime to $x$. Hence the greedy scan accepts $x$, proving $S\\in\\mathcal F$.",
  "status_as_written": "established",
  "repair_distance": "none",
  "explanation": "The objection correctly notes the reverse direction of (2) (upward closure of F) is not spelled out at the quoted place. But the displayed self-duality (1) is proved in full immediately before: if S ⊇ C with C ∈ F, then by (1) C meets every R ∈ F, hence so does S, hence S ∈ F by (1) again. The characterization L6.1 is therefore established in the text; the omission is a one-inference cosmetic gap, not a missing case, and later uses of (2) rest on the proved equivalence (1)."
